headline: OpenRAC adds multiplayer world APIs, warm savestates and installable map packs
summary: Native mods gain Ratchet & Clank player poses, shared-world controls and pages in the game's menus, alongside same-process savestates (#86). Creators can export edited Godot worlds as map packs and launch them through Mods, though #84 supplies tools rather than an authored map. Experimental interior lighting and Novalis water also land, with the author warning that interiors can still be too dark and need tuning (#74). Master again takes direct development work rather than only a release pull request, and a history rewrite leaves one commit range unavailable from GitHub.
highlights: Mod SDK 1.5.0 and 1.7.0 are released. Later master code extends the mod interface through 1.9 for sharing the game's world.
PAL level edits now target the 60 Hz gameplay copy the native game loads (#87). The launcher shows prepared level files, asset packs and recorded edits (#91).
Movies use the game's language, the camera follows the departing ship, and NTSC-U fixes address object updates and a skipped-frame effect-texture crash (#98, #96, #93, #95).
Large PAL and NTSC-U source updates mostly import upstream names, structures and implementations. Port-specific replacements remain where newly imported source cannot run as written.
Going Commando gains boot/title/menu C comparison tools (#85) and can build from the player's disc image. Its launcher Play action remains developer-only behind a warning.
Custom ship destinations and packaged editor layouts close without merging (#92, #94). The incomplete GitHub commit comparison means the recovered commit list is not exhaustive.
